ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle XYZ, with top side XZ being a horizontal line segment, labeled with length 30; point Y is below, and the two left and right slanted sides XY and YZ are both labeled 17, so the triangle in the figure is an isosceles triangle, with side lengths 17, 17, 30. Reasoning: Draw the altitude from Y to the base XZ in the isosceles triangle in the figure. The altitude of an isosceles triangle bisects the base, so the base 30 is divided into 15 and 15. Thus a right triangle is obtained, with hypotenuse 17, one leg 15, and height sqrt(17^2 - 15^2) = sqrt(289 - 225) = sqrt(64) = 8. The area is 30 × 8 / 2 = 120, consistent with the problem statement. Using the same 8-15-17 right triangle, interchange the two legs to construct another isosceles triangle: let the half-base be 8 and the height be 15, then the full base is 16, and the two equal legs are still 17. The area of this triangle is 16 × 15 / 2 = 120, and all side lengths are integers. The problem states that there are two such isosceles triangles with integer side lengths, so this is the second triangle. Its perimeter is 17 + 17 + 16 = 50.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: triangle XYZ is isosceles with equal slanted sides XY = YZ = 17 and top base XZ = 30. From the text, its area is 120 and there is exactly one other integer-sided isosceles triangle with area 120. Drop the altitude from Y to base XZ; because the triangle is isosceles, it bisects the base into 15 and 15. Use the right triangle with hypotenuse 17 and leg 15 to get height 8, matching area 30·8/2 = 120. Then use the same 8-15-17 right-triangle data with the legs swapped to construct the other isosceles triangle: take half-base 8 and height 15, so the full base is 16 and the equal sides are still 17. Its area is 16·15/2 = 120, and since the text says there are only two such triangles, this constructed one is the second. Perimeter = 17 + 17 + 16 = 50.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first to identify the displayed triangle as the integer-sided isosceles triangle with side lengths 17, 17, and 30. For a systematic search, let any integer-sided isosceles triangle with area 120 have equal sides a and base b. Dropping the altitude gives half-base b/2 and height h, so a^2 = h^2 + (b/2)^2 and 120 = bh/2. Equivalently, set c = 2h; then b·c = 480 and b^2 + c^2 = (2a)^2. Thus (b,c,2a) must be a right triangle with integer legs whose product is 480. Enumerate factor pairs of 480 and test which give a square sum: the valid pairs are (30,16) and (16,30), both giving hypotenuse 34, hence a = 17. The image shows the case b = 30, so the other triangle has b = 16 and equal sides 17. Its perimeter is 17 + 17 + 16 = 50.
